cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 1:1), is writing to Timothy, who he calls his child. Earlier in the letter, Paul says everyone in the province of Asia deserted him, but a man named Onesiphorus often refreshed him and wasn't ashamed of his chains (2 Timothy 1:15-16). Now Paul gives Timothy a charge: be STRONG.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to be strong. Strong in what?

answers.text: The grace that is in Christ Jesus
His own hard training and effort
The wisdom of the older leaders

cards.text: Everything Timothy heard Paul say in front of many witnesses, he's supposed to entrust to FAITHFUL men. Not just anybody, friend, but the kind you'd trust with the last batch in the oven.

cards.question: Timothy is to entrust Paul's teaching to faithful men. What should those men be qualified to do?

cards.text: Then Paul paints a picture. He wants Timothy to join him in something, right alongside him, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to join him in ___ like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

cards.text: A soldier doesn't get tangled up in civilian affairs. You will NEVER see a soldier in the middle of a mission go, "Hold on, hold on, HOLD ON, I gotta answer the group chat."

cards.question: A soldier stays out of civilian affairs. Why does he do it?

answers.text: To please the one who enlisted him
To earn a higher rank someday
To keep himself out of danger

cards.text: Second picture: an athlete in a competition, going for the crown. Friend, the only race I've ever run is me against the oven timer, and that timer is UNDEFEATED.

cards.question: A competitor doesn't receive the crown unless he competes according to the ___.

cards.text: Third picture: a farmer. He works hard in his field, and then the crops come in.

cards.question: Paul says the hardworking farmer should be the last to partake of the crops.
Soldier, athlete, farmer. Paul tells Timothy to consider what he's saying. Who will give Timothy insight into all things?

cards.text: Now Paul gets to the heart of it. He tells Timothy to remember Jesus Christ, descended from David, just as Paul's gospel proclaims.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead.

cards.text: That gospel is why Paul is suffering, chained like a criminal. Friend, I spent years stuck in the back of a drawer, and even I never had it THAT rough.

cards.question: Paul is chained like a criminal for the gospel. What does he say cannot be chained?
Paul endures all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain ___.

cards.text: That salvation is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory. Not the kind of glory that's gone by Tuesday, friend. ETERNAL.

Then Paul shares a trustworthy saying about Christ Jesus, and every line comes in a pair: if we died with Him, we'll also live with Him, and if we endure, we'll also reign with Him. Friend, that's the kind of promise you tape right to the oven door.

cards.question: Paul's trustworthy saying about Christ Jesus isn't only comfort. One line is a warning. Which one?

answers.text: If we deny Him He will also deny us
If we rest He will take our crown
If we doubt Him He will walk away

cards.text: And then the last line of Paul's saying about Christ Jesus: if we are faithless, He remains faithful. Friend, read that one again. Slowly.

cards.question: In Paul's trustworthy saying, Christ Jesus remains faithful even if we are faithless. Why?
